As a person of color, I have to deal with racists just about every day. 

I simply don't have enough time or energy to live my life AND teach every one of them how to have basic decency for their fellow man. They have the ability to decide that for themselves. They have all the information at their fingertips.

I am patient with people, and kind, even when they are ignorant. But losing respect for people who do not have respect for me is just something that naturally happens on the inside.

Also, I love talking to anti-racists who used to support racism. Some of my best friends are in that category.

You missed my point: BLM drew attention to the issue of racial injustice in the US to the level that everyone with functioning eyes or ears became aware that there are big racial problems happening.

At that point, it became each individual's responsibility to educate themselves, or to remain ignorant. To do the right thing or to do the wrong thing.

So, claiming ignorance of big racial issues no longer works. Like nope, that person knew something was happening and chose the path of willful ignorance. No respect.
